# CsvDelimiterInvalidByteLength

<Badge type="danger" text="error" /> <Badge type="tip" text="native" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Use a one-byte CSV separator.

## Example

Finding:

```php{2}
<?php
fgetcsv($fp, 0, "::");
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 2: Use a one-byte CSV separator.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- For resolved fgetcsv, fputcsv, str_getcsv (PHP 5.3+) and SplFileObject CSV methods/setCsvControl, report an explicitly provided separator whose constant string length is not exactly one byte. Use byte length, not Unicode scalar length.
- Emit one finding per violating operation. Flow facts require a reachable path with no intervening mutation, escaped alias or unknown call involving the tracked value. When the proof is inconclusive, nothing is reported.

## Exceptions (no report)

- Omitted default separator and unknown strings are excluded. A single-byte non-ASCII value is legal; UTF-8 multibyte separators are not.
- Exclude shadowed builtin symbols, unresolved required types, incomplete syntax and unsupported PHP versions.

## Fix

No automatic fix. Choosing a repair requires runtime information, error-handling policy or a semantic decision.

## PHP versions

Available throughout PHP 5.3–8.5.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "CsvDelimiterInvalidByteLength": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore CsvDelimiterInvalidByteLength
```
